transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Aisha (CSM) -- Priya (CTO), Liam (Head of Security), Sofia (Infra), Ethan (Product)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on security posture and deployment preferences (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer wants encryption/KMS details, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC model, audit logging retention, and SOC2/ISO artifacts. They are leaning to a private or dedicated deployment because of PCI/PDPA constraints but open to hosted if we can satisfy key controls.

Topics: SOC2/ISO certs; SSO/SAML + SCIM; KMS/customer-managed keys; RBAC and least-privilege; audit logs and retention; data at rest vs in transit; private VPC/on-prem options; performance trade-offs and fallbacks.

[00:00] Maya: all right hey everyone thanks for joining on valentines day, sorry for the cheesy time but we'll try to keep tight, um quick intros?
[00:06] Priya: hi i'm priya, cto at sable, we run the personalization engine and, uh, concern first is cardholder data and retention, compliance to pci, and pdpa for SEA markets.
[00:13] Liam: liam here head of security, i'll focus on controls and auditability.
[00:17] Jonas: jonas, se at redwood, i'll cover infra and perf questions.
[00:22] Sofia: sofia infra, i'll likely run the pilot and provide traffic patterns.

[00:45] Ethan: quick note, timeline is Q2 pilot and we'd like security sign-off before any customer-facing rollout.

[01:12] Maya: perfect — wanted to frame the call: we'll cover compliance artifacts we can share, how SSO works with our console, options for KMS (hosted vs customer-managed), audit logs, and deployment modes. then we'll capture next steps.

[02:05] Liam: first question: do you have SOC2 type II and ISO 27001? and are those third-party audited?
[02:14] Maya: yes we are SOC2 type II, and iso 27001 certified; both are third-party audited. i will drop links to the reports, redactions applied of course.
[02:25] Liam: ok, will need the control matrix. also are pen tests available?
[02:31] Ravi: we do annual pen tests, and will share the summary report; if you need more detail we can sign an nda.

[03:03] Priya: on auth: we use okta with SAML and SCIM for provisioning. how straightforward is SSO and provisioning?
[03:12] Jonas: we support SAML SSO for the console and SCIM provisioning for users and groups. typical flow is SAML for auth and SCIM to sync groups into our RBAC. small caveat — mapping custom attributes sometimes needs a quick mapping doc.
[03:28] Sofia: does SCIM push group membership into your RBAC? we want least-priv priv model and per-team namespaces.
[03:35] Jonas: yes scim syncs groups, and our RBAC supports teams and resource-level roles, you can do project-level admins and read-only viewer roles. we also support attribute-based access for some fields.

[04:10] Liam: audit logs — what events do you capture? retention windows? can we export logs to our splunk/elk?
[04:20] Maya: standard audit events: logins, api key creation/rotation, model deploys, rollout changes, prompts flagged for eval, and system alerts. hosted retains 90 days by default but we can extend. for dedicated/private deployments you can keep logs in your splunk via forwarder or s3 export, retention then controlled by you.
[04:44] Ethan: and are logs tamper-evident or signed? we need chain of custody.
[04:49] Jonas: for hosted we append cryptographic checksums and we have immutable append-only stores for audit trails; for private you control the store so chain of custody is via your infra. we'll provide detail in the security packet.

[05:30] Priya: encryption: do you support customer-managed keys (cmk) in cloud kms? and for on-prem HSM?
[05:40] Ravi: yes we support CMKs via major cloud KMS (aws kms, gcp kms, azure key vault) and we have integrations with external HSMs for private deployments. keys can be configured to be customer-owned and we never store plaintext model keys.
[05:56] Liam: about data at rest vs tokenization — when a request hits the api, do you ever persist request payloads? what's default retention?
[06:05] Maya: hosted api: we persist minimal metadata and ephemeral request logs for 30 days by default for debugging; we have a strict opt-out and data retention controls — you can opt-out of persistent storage and enable ephemeral-only which keeps only in-memory for the request lifecycle. for dedicated/private deployments, by default nothing leaves your VPC unless you opt-in.

[06:40] Sofia: how does private deployment work network-wise — do we get a control plane connection back to your managed control plane? we have air-gap concerns.
[06:50] Jonas: two private models: a fully air-gapped on-prem bundle (no egress, requires local management) and a VPC private deployment where a control plane signals via a secure mTLS channel. for your pci use-case we can evaluate the air-gap package; it's heavier ops but removes external control plane dependency.

[07:20] Priya: performance tradeoffs — what latency overhead should we expect on-prem vs hosted?
[07:29] Jonas: hosted we've optimized to single-digit token latencies for many models; dedicated gives predictability, and private on-prem incurs overheads depending on hardware and networking — rough estimate is 5–30% additional latency vs cloud optimized instances if you have comparable GPUs.

[08:05] Ethan: about fallbacks — if capacity in dedicated hits a limit, do you have automatic fallback to hosted? and how does that affect data flow?
[08:16] Maya: yes we have policy-based fallbacks. but for customers with strict data residency we can disable fallbacks; otherwise fallback routes to compatible variants and we annotate logs to show when fallback occurred. fallback can be configured to scrub sensitive fields.

[09:10] Liam: RBAC review — can we integrate with our existing idp groups and map to granular permissions? are there audit-ready roles?
[09:20] Jonas: yes okta groups map via scim; we provide roles like admin, deployer, billing, viewer. you can create custom roles but note some deep ops privileges are restricted to specific roles. we'll share the RBAC matrix.

[10:05] Priya: data residency — we have customers in singapore and indonesia — can you guarantee region data stays in ap-southeast-1?
[10:15] Maya: hosted supports regional hosting and region pinning for models and data. for guaranteed residency we recommend dedicated in that region or private deployment inside your cloud account.

[11:02] Sofia: about key rotation and access — if our KMS rotates keys do you support re-encrypting stored artifacts?
[11:12] Ravi: yes we support key rotation workflows; for stored artifacts re-encryption can be orchestrated with a rotation job. for large datasets we recommend using envelope encryption. we'll send our key rotation playbook.

[12:00] Ethan: can you provide a list of sub-processors and data flow diagram? legal will need it.
[12:08] Maya: yes we'll include the sub-processor list and a sanitized data flow diagram in the packet.

[13:40] Liam: incident response SLA — how fast do you notify customers and what detail?
[13:48] Aisha: we have tiered incident response: SEV1 notify in 1 hour, postmortem in 72 hours for production incidents. we include list of impacted customers, root cause, and mitigation. for private deployments incident ops are handled locally but we provide runbooks and remote support as agreed.

[15:10] Priya: curious about evaluation: we want to run a 2-week pilot under a dev dataset, send 50k tokens/day, and measure p95 latency and throughput. will that be possible on dedicated?
[15:22] Jonas: yes we can provision a small dedicated pool for the pilot, or we can spin up a private dev cluster in your account. for benchmarking we'll need the exact traffic shape. sofia can share that.

[16:00] Sofia: i'll share JSON of traffic, token size distribution, and concurrency numbers.

[16:20] Maya: on pricing — we'll give a draft for dedicated and private and a hosted baseline. if you can share projected monthly tokens and SLA needs we'll model it.

[17:05] Priya: any references or customers in retail space who have done private deployments?
[17:12] Maya: yes, we'll anonymize a case study and share architecture patterns and what trade-offs they accepted.

[18:00] Liam: a few nitty-gritty: do you support SAML assertion expiry shorter than default? and do you rotate session tokens?
[18:08] Jonas: assertion expiry can be tuned via idp policy, and session tokens rotate on a 1-hour sliding window by default; we can shorten for compliance.

[19:00] Ethan: what's the support model during pilot? dedicated SE and CSM?
[19:06] Aisha: yes pilot comes with SE support (on-call) and weekly syncs; escalation path is included in the pilot agreement.

[20:00] Maya: recap: we'll send SOC2 + ISO links, security packet (KMS, pen test summary, rbac matrix), network diagram options for private vs vpc, and draft pricing. jonas will prepare perf checklist and test plan; will schedule 60-min deep dive next week.

[20:20] Priya: sounds good. can we get the security packet by monday?
[20:25] Maya: we'll target monday 2026-02-16.

[20:40] Liam: one last thing — retention policy: we need 90 days for audit logs, and for prompt data we require 0 retention by default unless explicitly opt-in. can you accomodate?
[20:52] Jonas: yes hosted default can be adjusted; for dedicated/private you control retention and we will make sure prompt storage is opt-in.

[21:30] Maya: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet and scheduling link.

[21:45] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: some names and acronyms may be slightly off (okta spelled as octa sometimes, scim as skim in auto transcription), timestamps approximate.
